_comment: Recording of live run 39 (status done); the plan is the model's own words.

steps.message: Reviewing the intake and the question.

claims.text: Goal entered: cut grid electricity 30% by 2030 at Red Hook Recreation Center (NYC Parks), 155 Bay Street, Brooklyn, with a $750,000 capital budget for 2027 and cooling-center loads kept running in outages.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: Efficiency only (Scenario A) does not reach the 30% goal: it covers about 21-59% of the goal (a 6.2-17.6% cut in annual use). Typical cost range $65,824-$226,165, within budget. It gives no backup power.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: Efficiency plus a smaller solar array within budget (Scenario B) reaches the goal on paper (a 50.8-66.6% cut in annual use). Typical cost range $418,771-$750,000. It gives no backup power because solar panels shut off in an outage without a battery.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: The full path (Scenario C: deeper efficiency, whole-roof solar and a backup battery) is the only option that keeps critical loads running in an outage, about 8.0-9.4 hours on the estimated critical load. It reaches the goal on paper (96.7-100% cut) but costs $163,245-$771,783 more than the $750,000 budget. Meeting both the goal and the outage need may take more than the budget; whether to extend it is a decision for the owner once the gap is compared with the savings.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: Roof solar alone could offset about 87-96% of annual use on paper, but the city's solar-readiness record says the roof is not solar ready and the roof condition is unknown. Roof structure and condition must be confirmed by a licensed engineer or architect and a roofer before any of the solar figures are relied on. Savings are estimates with ranges, and no outcome is assured.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: User-entered profile: park recreation center built 1936, 27,069 sq ft, flat roof of 32,860 sq ft, Con Edison customer, annual electricity use 375,066 kWh (kWh = energy over time), critical loads are gym cooling, lighting and communications for a cooling center.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: The city's energy-reporting record (Local Law 84, report year 2024) shows 375,066 kWh of electricity, matching the entered figure, and about 3,073,752 kBtu (thousand BTU) of natural gas. The electricity figure is treated as measured. Gas heating is outside an electricity-use goal, so the 30% goal covers electricity only.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: The city's tax-lot record lists 21,600 sq ft of gross floor area, while the user entered 27,069 sq ft (the energy-reporting record also shows 27,069). The user's figure is kept as the working figure; please confirm. The record is filed under 140 Lorraine Street, while the address asked about is 155 Bay Street. This can be another frontage of the same lot; both addresses are shown here.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: City building outlines on the lot total about 32,862 sq ft across 4 buildings (27,000; 4,370; 825 and 667 sq ft), close to the 32,860 sq ft roof the user entered. An outline is ground area, not a measured roof, and several of these buildings may not be part of the recreation center. Roof area stays the user's number and must be verified by an engineer or roofer.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: The city record marks the lot as a landmark, and the profile shows NYC Parks parkland.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: Existing systems: the intake did not list any existing solar, renewables or efficiency work, so this plan assumes none. However, the city's solar-readiness record lists 11.4 kW of installed solar (about 12,540 kWh a year). If that array is already on this roof, the free roof area and the solar figures here are smaller. Please confirm what is already installed. If LED lighting or controls are already done, the efficiency savings are lower.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: Solar output range: system losses of 18% (low) to 10% (high) around the solar model's 14% default; weather is typical-year data.
claims.label: ASSUMPTION

claims.text: Usable roof setback factor of 0.55 (only 55% of the roof is treated as usable for panels).
claims.label: ASSUMPTION

claims.text: Array density of 66 sq ft of roof per kW (kW = how much power at one moment) of solar.
claims.label: ASSUMPTION

claims.text: Critical load was not given, so it is estimated at 1.0 W per sq ft x 27,069 sq ft = 27.1 kW (a planning estimate, not metered). Backup length was not given, so 8 hours is assumed. Battery energy = kW x hours / 0.85 round-trip efficiency = 255 kWh.
claims.label: ASSUMPTION

claims.text: Efficiency measures (LED and controls) save 10-20% of annual use. This is a planning estimate, not a cited benchmark and not a building model.
claims.label: ASSUMPTION

claims.text: Benchmark prices are planning-level, not quotes: solar $2,528-3,752 per kW and battery $546-812 per kWh (the middle half of similar completed NYC projects, NYSERDA data), efficiency $1.17-4.02 per kWh saved a year (standard) and $1.09-3.83 (deep). The efficiency savings percents are planning estimates, and only 62-88% of them is counted because the City's audited projects delivered that share (Local Law 87 report, DCAS FY2022).
claims.label: ASSUMPTION

claims.text: The baseline for the goal is the electricity the building buys from the grid: 375,066 kWh a year, treated as measured (it matches the city's energy-reporting record). A 30% cut is about 112,520 kWh a year. No existing efficiency or solar work was entered, so none is taken into account.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: A standard efficiency package (LED lighting and controls) is estimated to cut about 6.2-17.6% of annual use (23,254-66,012 kWh a year). This counts only 62-88% of the predicted savings, because the City's own audited projects delivered that share. The underlying 10-20% savings is a planning estimate, not a measured result for this building.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: Lighting type, cooling equipment and whether building controls exist were not entered. An energy audit is recommended to find out which efficiency measures remain, particularly for gym cooling, since cooling is a critical load.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Usable roof area is about 18,073 sq ft (32,860 sq ft x 0.55). Roof area is the user's number and must be verified with an engineer or roofer.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: A whole-roof array would be about 273.8 kW DC (18,073 sq ft / 66 sq ft per kW).
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: Estimated solar output for the whole-roof array is 327,822-360,189 kWh a year (about 344,031 kWh central), for a flat roof at a 10 degree tilt facing south. The range comes from the assumed loss band.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: That output equals about 92% of annual use (about 0.92 at the central value). Roof solar alone would then exceed the 30% goal on paper, but only if the roof can carry the array.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: Estimated whole-roof solar savings are $64,941-$87,094 a year (low output at the low price, to high output at the high price), using the New York commercial average price.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: The city's solar-readiness record says this site is not solar ready, and gives no roof condition or age. No cost total here includes repairing or replacing the roof; a roofer's quote is needed. If the roof is replaced or renovated, the city's sustainable roofs rule (Local Laws 92 and 94 of 2019) requires solar, a green roof or both over the applicable roof.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: Simple payback is used throughout, not a full financial model. Surplus solar is not part of any figure.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: Scenario A (efficiency only): reduction 6.2-17.6% of annual use, 21-59% of the goal, does not reach the goal. Upfront cost $65,824-$226,165 (median of similar NYC projects about $144,025); net cost the same, since no credit applies. Payback 4.1-49.1 years. Within budget (9-30% of it). Outage hours: none.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: Scenario B (efficiency plus a 139.6 kW solar array sized to the budget): reduction 50.8-66.6% of annual use, 169-222% of the goal, reaches the goal. Upfront cost $418,771-$750,000 (median about $562,870); net cost $312,887-$592,849 after the federal credit (median about $437,217). Payback 5.2-15.7 years. Within budget (56-100% of it). Outage hours: none, because there is no battery.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: Scenario C (deeper efficiency, 273.8 kW solar and a 255 kWh battery): reduction 96.7-100% of annual use, reaches the goal. Upfront cost $913,245-$1,521,783 (median about $1,183,468); net cost $663,801-$1,151,438 after the federal credit (median about $884,462). Payback 7.3-16.0 years. Over budget: the estimated cost is $163,245-$771,783 more than the budget. Outage hours 8.0-9.4.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: In Scenario C the roof could produce up to about 67,637 kWh a year more than the building uses. That surplus would flow to the grid, is not counted in the savings, and depends on net-metering rules that were not checked.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: The budget gap in Scenario C is measured against upfront cost. After the federal credit, the lowest net cost ($663,801) would be inside $750,000, but the credit comes after the work is paid for, and its eligibility for this agency is not confirmed.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: The budget is entered as a capital amount for 2027. The model treats it as one total upfront figure, so it is not modeled year by year.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: Scenario C, expanded efficiency package: typical range $81,764-$287,301; the median of similar NYC projects is about $186,783. Based on 75,013 kWh saved a year at $1.09-3.83 per kWh saved (the middle half of completed NYC public-sector projects, NYSERDA data). The 15-25% savings is a planning estimate.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: Scenario C, rooftop solar: typical range $692,251-$1,027,423; the median of similar NYC projects is about $821,500. Based on 273.8 kW x $2,528-3,752 per kW (the middle half of 239 completed NYC non-residential projects of 100-500 kW since 2022, NYSERDA data). This is a real project price range, not a quote.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: Scenario C, backup battery: typical range $139,230-$207,060; the median of similar NYC projects is about $175,185. Based on 255 kWh x $546-812 per kWh (the middle half of 56 completed or approved NYC commercial-scale storage projects, NYSERDA data). The battery size rests on an estimated load and an assumed 8 hours.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: Scenario C, federal credit (30% of solar and battery): -$249,444 to -$370,345 (about -$299,005 at the median). Counted because the IRS page lists the program as open for governmental entities, with solar placed in service by 2027-12-31. Whether this agency and project qualify is not confirmed, and the placed-in-service date is tight against a 2027 budget year.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: The NY-Sun commercial solar incentive could not be confirmed: NYSERDA's dashboard blocks automated reading, so its current status is uncertain. It is left out of every net cost. Check the dashboard in a browser before counting any incentive.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: The sustainable roofs rule (Local Laws 92 and 94 of 2019) is a rule, not an incentive, and no dollar value is counted for it.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: None of the cost totals include roof repair or replacement, flood protection work, or Landmarks-related design changes. A roofer's quote and an engineer's scope are needed.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Phase 0, confirm data and budget: confirm the floor area (27,069 vs 21,600 sq ft), what solar or efficiency work already exists (the city lists 11.4 kW), the real critical load in kW and backup hours wanted, the roof replacement year, the budget year and whether $750,000 is total or annual, and the tariff from a Con Edison bill.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Phase 1, professional reviews: a licensed structural PE or RA to analyze the roof structure, and a roof condition survey (age, drainage, repair or replacement before solar). The roof cannot be certified from these records.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Phase 2, efficiency measures: an energy audit, then the efficiency package (LED lighting if not already done, controls, cooling upgrades). It cuts the baseline before solar and battery are sized, which can shrink the battery and array.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Phase 3, permits and interconnection: agency approvals and Landmarks review, Department of Buildings permits, a licensed electrician, FDNY rooftop access review, and a Con Edison interconnection application. Start early given the federal credit's end-of-2027 placed-in-service date.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Phase 4, solar installation: install the array the roof review supports. Scenario B (about 139.6 kW) fits the budget; the whole roof (about 273.8 kW) is Scenario C. The owner decides whether to extend the budget after comparing the gap with the savings.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Phase 5, battery, commissioning and verification: install the battery above flood level, commission the backup transfer, then compare the first 12 months of Con Edison bills with the estimates here.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Scenario C gives about 8.0-9.4 hours of backup for the critical loads: gym cooling, lighting and communications for the cooling center. Scenarios A and B give no backup power; solar panels shut off in an outage without a battery.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: The battery (255 kWh, 27.1 kW) rests on an estimated critical load and an assumed 8 hours, not metered data. Running gym cooling through a heat wave may need more than 27.1 kW, so a metered critical-load list is needed before sizing.
claims.label: ASSUMPTION

claims.text: FEMA's current flood map puts this address in zone AE, a special flood hazard area (the center flooded in Hurricane Sandy). Only the flood zone was read; heat and winter-storm ratings were not looked up, and the 2015 preliminary flood map was not checked. NYC code uses the more restrictive map.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: Flood protection: put the battery, inverters and switchgear on the roof or elevated above the design flood elevation, and have a flood-zone review done under NYC Building Code Appendix G.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Structural analysis by a licensed PE or RA is required. The roof cannot be certified from these records, and a roof condition survey is also required, because the city lists the site as not solar ready.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Licensed electrician, FDNY rooftop access review, and Con Edison interconnection review are required for rooftop solar and a battery.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Landmark site: the city record shows a landmark flag, so a Landmarks Preservation Commission review is needed before rooftop or exterior work. Because the site is both a landmark and on parkland, the Commission gives the owning agency an advisory report, not a permit.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Parkland: a parkland use review by counsel is needed, and NYC Parks is the owning agency whose approval is required.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Flood-zone review under NYC Building Code Appendix G is required for equipment in zone AE.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

sections.title: Path to net-zero and learning resources

claims.text: Electricity could approach net zero on paper with Scenario C (96.7-100% cut in grid purchases), but the building also uses about 3,073,752 kBtu of natural gas a year. Net-zero for the whole building would need a separate heating plan, which this electricity goal does not model.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: A staged approach is suggested: efficiency first, then solar sized to what the roof review supports, then the battery. The list at the end of the plan has official pages for NYSERDA, Con Edison, the Department of Buildings and others.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Floor area conflict: the user entered 27,069 sq ft; the city tax-lot record shows 21,600 sq ft. The user's figure is the working figure; please confirm.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: Address mismatch: the city record is filed under 140 Lorraine Street, while 155 Bay Street was asked about. It may be another frontage of the same lot; the building records may not be for the exact address.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: Existing systems were not entered; this plan assumes none, yet the city lists 11.4 kW of installed solar. Please confirm. Roof replacement year, roof condition, lighting type, cooling type, controls, heating fuel, critical load in kW and backup hours were also left blank, which lowers confidence in the solar, battery and efficiency figures.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: The electricity price is the New York commercial average ($0.1981-$0.2418 per kWh), not this building's own tariff. Several Con Edison general-service tariffs exist for NYC; the building's own tariff must be confirmed on a bill, and savings use the state average.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: The incentive list is a register kept by a person, with each official page re-read by the system. NY-Sun status could not be confirmed and is left out of net cost. The federal credit is counted as open, but whether this agency qualifies is not confirmed.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: Only the flood zone was read; heat and winter-storm ratings were not looked up and the 2015 preliminary flood map was not checked.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: Efficiency savings percents are planning estimates, not project data; only 62-88% of them is counted. Solar and battery prices are the middle half of similar completed NYC projects, not quotes. Payback is a simple payback. The Scenario C budget gap is measured against upfront cost.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: No scenario combines solar with a battery inside the $750,000 budget; Scenario B has no battery. A middle option (smaller array plus a smaller battery) was not modeled and can be run once the critical load and roof review are known.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Savings cannot be promised; every figure in this plan is an estimate with a range.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

roadmap.footer_note: All figures are planning estimates with ranges, not quotes. Roof structure and condition must be confirmed by a licensed PE or RA and a roofer before any solar spending.
